Why didn't the new Houston team pick the Oilers name back up like the Browns did?

The Browns move to Baltimore was the first time that the NFL insisted on keeping the team name and records in the original city. Prior to that, every move included moving the team name and records. Since it was prior, the owner of the Oilers, Bud Adams, got to keep the trademarks and copyrights for all things Oilers. This is why on occasion, the Titans will wear Oiler jerseys as throwback uniforms. It's also why the Ravens were born, because owner Robert Irsay took the Colts logo, record, and jerseys away from Baltimore when they moved to Indiana in the middle of the night. It appears that going forward, the league will do things the way they did with Cleveland, since it's so painful for Houston Oilers fans and Baltimore Colts fans to see their team's gear being paraded around a new city as if it had been there the whole time, and not a part of the original city's identity.
